children: could see faster revenue growth over the next several years as it works through a $638 billion backlog of contracted business, despite pressure from heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The cloud company reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $67.4 billion, up 17% from a year earlier. Cloud infrastructure revenue increased 77% to $18.1 billion, while the remaining performance obligation, or RPO, reached $638 billion in the fourth quarter.

Oracle expects to recognize about 12% of that backlog over the next 12 months and another 34% during the following 13 to 36 months. The company projects fiscal 2027 revenue of more than $90 billion, representing growth of about 34%.

Oracle is also seeking customer prepayments and arrangements in which clients provide their own hardware to help manage capital requirements. The company said it signed $67 billion of new contracts in the fourth quarter, with most involving those structures.
Analysts expect earnings growth to strengthen in later fiscal years as more backlog converts into revenue. Oracle trades at about 19 times forward earnings, below the Nasdaq-100's 25 multiple.
Oracale stock has fallen about 17% in 2026, lagging the broader market index.

title: Oracle Bets Big on AI With $638 Billion Backlog as Stock Struggles
